subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue any of these requested native core surfaces now: file/search batching, AI-callable context blocks, or runner-enforced submitted plans?
rationale: The request changes core tool schemas, context/session semantics, and config/enforcement policy, while VISION.md only partially aligns and cautions against heavy orchestration layers or optional capability that can live through plugin/API seams.

options.title: Split for design review
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

options.title: Route pieces to plugins or existing APIs
options.body: Defer core changes unless a specific plugin/API gap is proven, using Parallel Search, context-engine plugins, and current planning UI where adequate.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Decide that native batching, AI-controlled context blocks, and strict plan enforcement are not planned for core at this time.

recommendation.title: Split for design review
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent history on structured planning, strict-agentic behavior, and central tool registration surfaces.
